svg.title: Proving a CR redraw prefix obsolete with isSpanObsolete
svg.desc: One prepared text run holds three same-row progress redraws starting at column 1 of a 32-column, 8-row terminal: "copy 12% [# ]", CR, "copy 57% [### ]", CR, "copy 100% [#####]". A forward scan proves each update is printable ASCII, does not wrap and covers the previous one (16 ≤ 16 ≤ 17 < 32), so isSpanObsolete(index, overwrite) returns true with cut 33, the final CR. The first 33 bytes are ghosted and never executed. The VT executes the retained CR and prints the replacement cell by cell, reaching the same cells, cursor and last character after running 18 of 51 bytes. The example is shortened for legibility; the implementation only attempts the proof for updates of at least 64 bytes.

g.text: Three same-row redraws of a progress line arrive in one text run.
Scan forward: printable ASCII from column 1, each covers the last, none wraps.
16 ≤ 16 ≤ 17 < 32 columns: bytes 0–32 are obsolete. Cut = 33, the final CR.
Two updates and their CR are never executed. No cells are written.
The retained CR returns to column 1 and closes the prior grapheme.
copy 100% [#####] is printed normally, cell by cell.
Same cells, cursor and last char as full execution. 18 of 51 bytes run.
